correctness.rationale: For fixed membership bits of the two terminals, an internal vertex fails the two-neighbor condition precisely at the center of a 101 word. Path choices therefore factor until the two terminal checks: at an omitted terminal the sum of incident internal bits is at most one, enforced by retaining powers zero and one of its marker, and at a selected terminal no restriction remains. Length two is included: its single internal bit marks both endpoints but contributes only one z. A two-bit transfer rejects only 10→01 and checks the final triple with the prescribed right terminal. At equal length three the cases with neither, one, and both terminals contribute (1+rz)^2, 2z[(1+z)^r+rz²(1+z)^(r−1)], and z²(1+z²)^r. In the single-terminal case the internal neighbor at the excluded terminal can be selected only in one arm and then forces its companion. With both terminals selected each pair is 00 or 11. The first two contributions cover degrees 0 through r+2; the last covers the even degrees from 2 through 2r+2. As 2r>r+2 for r≥3, only the paired case yields a proper set of size 2r, exactly one choice per omitted arm, and degree 2r+1 is absent. The full set is unique and evaluation at one gives the stated total. Independent vertex-mask tests against a separate arm-word calculation returned all matching coefficients: for lengths (2,3,4,5) the total is 410, and for seven length-three arms it is 1344 with seven maximum proper sets.
residual_risks: The finite replay supports only its tested instances. The membership-factor proof supplies the general result.
The simple graph, arm length and labelled-subset hypotheses matter; nothing follows here for extra terminal edges, overlapping interiors, or identification modulo symmetry.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Cacti exclude the overlapping cycles from three parallel arms. A one-subdivision formula cannot cover the entire theta family: in the equal-length-three case the terminal vertices have degree at least three and must be original, but the path between original vertices along any completely subdivided arm has even length. A broader algorithm to evaluate counts on inputs is not an explicit parametric coefficient or support theorem.

equivalent_formulations.reasoning: A complement-size polynomial simply reverses the coefficients, so such a match on the same family would count. Cyclic prisms are not theta networks: all their vertices are cubic, whereas theta networks here have precisely two vertices of degree above two.

value.rationale: The size distribution is a natural refinement of the established counting problem on a basic graph family with overlapping cycles. The all-length product works with shared terminal capacities; the closed form in the uniform family discriminates attainable sizes and classifies all largest proper sets. The value lies in that exact structural information, not in isolated numbers or in using a transfer alone.
residual_risks: The binomial support result is for length three, not arbitrary path lengths or series-parallel graphs.
